correctness.rationale: Two-vertex Bloch cells give off-diagonal product Z=(c cos θ+2ir sin θ)^2+d^2 sin²θ at the first nonconstant mode, with c=a+b, d=a−b, θ=2π/N. For X=c² cos²θ and Y=(d²−4r²)sin²θ, |Z|²−(X−Y)²=4Xd²sin²θ, so the square root with nonnegative real part has real part at least c cos θ. The other spectral obstruction is the alternating eigenvector in the constant-cell block, with eigenvalue 1−2c. Their maximum bound has its unique minimum at c=2/(3−cos θ), and the homogeneous reversible spectrum attains it. For even N≥6, at this c the first bound is strict for d≠0 by the identity, and for d=0,r≠0 by the imaginary part. For N=4 the two nonconstant-cell eigenvalues are 1−c±√(d²−4r²), whose maximum modulus exceeds 1−c unless the discriminant is zero, whether it is real positive or negative. Balancing against |1−2c| yields exactly c=2/3 and d²=4r²; then |r|≤1/6. The example has nonconstant-cell block with diagonals 1/3 and off-diagonals 1/3,0, establishing geometric multiplicity one. The invariant mean-zero subspace counts extra eigenvalues 1 in reducible cases. The supplied SymPy identities and witness and 2275 finite grid iterations were inspected, not rerun; the grid does not prove an optimum on the continuous domain.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: One cannot combine separate inequalities for r=0 and d=0 into a bound for d and r both nonzero. value.rationale: Period two is the simplest nonconstant periodic symmetric environment in which circulation can interact with inhomogeneity. The sharp bound gives a tractable global case beyond the separate-perturbation and local comparisons. Its four-cycle exception provides a whole explicit family showing that even attainment of the optimal spectral modulus need not imply reversibility or diagonalizability; this distinction matters for finite-time behavior.
